context: Request: the most recent closed M&A deal with disclosure schedules to use as a template. The log header names no matters; the criteria require 1006-00008 (Crestline Packaging APA signed June 16, 2025, closed August 15, 2025) and its disclosure-schedules.docx, and nothing else as qualifying. Other closed deals with schedules (1006-00006 closed July 31, 2025; 1003-00003 July 22, 2025; 1038-00008 July 18, 2025; 1001-00007 April 2025) are older.

divergence: All three runs fail, each differently. T0 found the right deal and proved its closing date, but its answer also listed three slightly older closed deals as backup templates in a comparison table, after reviews asked it to name and date the comparison matters (over-inclusion, review-endorsed). T1 read only a closing letter of the right deal and listed its folder, never opened its closing certificate, and answered with an April 2025 deal while calling the right one unverified (under-inclusion). T2 read the right deal's agreement, schedules and checklist but ranked another deal first, and the run ended in a context overflow before any answer was written. That run had opened with a 3.3M-character scan output and kept making large reads. Reviews flagged hand-picked candidate sets everywhere. Agent-defined stages were frequent in T0 (eleven verification and final-read stages, all mapped to existing stages) and did not remove the comparison rows.
